# Tutorial for spatial ordinal pattern tests

## Libraries

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| message: false
using StatsOrdinalPatterns, Random, Statistics, DataFrames, CairoMakie
```

## Hypothesis Testing with Spatial Ordinal Patterns

A spatial ordinal pattern (SOP) test asks whether the frequencies of rank permutations in a 2D image are consistent with a spatially i.i.d. process. For an $M \times N$ image, overlapping $2 \times 2$ windows at delays $(d_1, d_2)$ are each mapped to the permutation that describes the relative order of the four values. The resulting frequency distribution is summarised by a scalar test statistic. Under $H_0$ (spatial white noise) that distribution is uniform across all $4! = 24$ patterns.

`StatsOrdinalPatterns.jl` provides:

- **Computing the statistic**
    - [`stat_sop()`](../reference/stat_sop.qmd) — computes the chosen test statistic from the observed pattern frequencies.
- **Asymptotic inference**
    - [`test_sop()`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) — compares the statistic to an analytical critical value. Supports all image sizes.
- **Bootstrap inference**
    - [`bootstrap_sop()`](../reference/bootstrap_sop.qmd) — generates the empirical null distribution by 2D resampling.
    - [`test_sop_bootstrap()`](../reference/test_sop_bootstrap.qmd) — combines statistic computation and bootstrap inference in one call.

## Key functions

- **[`stat_sop(data, d1, d2; chart_choice, refinement=OrdinaryType())`](../reference/stat_sop.qmd)**

    - Returns `[test_statistic, pattern_frequencies]`.
    - `data`: the 2D image (`Matrix`). `d1`: row delay. `d2`: column delay.
    - `chart_choice`: one of [`TauTilde()`](../reference/TauTilde.qmd), [`TauHat()`](../reference/TauHat.qmd), [`KappaTilde()`](../reference/KappaTilde.qmd), [`KappaHat()`](../reference/KappaHat.qmd), [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](../reference/DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd), [`Shannon(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon), [`ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy).
    - `refinement`: [`OrdinaryType()`](../reference/OrdinaryType.qmd) for classical types, or [`RotationType()`](../reference/RotationType.qmd), [`DirectionType()`](../reference/DirectionType.qmd), [`DiagonalType()`](../reference/DiagonalType.qmd).

- **[`test_sop(data, d1, d2; chart_choice, refinement=OrdinaryType(), alpha=0.05)`](../reference/test_sop.qmd)**

    - Returns an [`SOPTestResult`](../reference/SOPTestResult.qmd) with the test statistic, critical value, p-value, and reject decision.
    - Critical value, p-value, and rejection direction are chosen automatically from `chart_choice`.
    - `alpha`: significance level.

- **[`bootstrap_sop(data, n_boot, d1, d2; chart_choice, refinement=OrdinaryType(), block_size=1)`](../reference/bootstrap_sop.qmd)**

    - Returns a length-`n_boot` vector of resampled statistics under $H_0$.
    - `block_size > 1`: 2D block bootstrap that preserves spatial structure.

- **[`test_sop_bootstrap(data, n_boot, d1, d2; chart_choice, refinement=OrdinaryType(), alpha=0.05, block_size=1)`](../reference/test_sop_bootstrap.qmd)**

    - Returns an [`SOPTestResultBoot`](../reference/SOPTestResultBoot.qmd) struct with the bootstrap critical value, p-value, and reject decision.
    - For Tau/Kappa charts: two-sided bootstrap using the raw statistic.
    - For entropy charts: the bootstrap null distribution is built on the same standardised scale used internally by [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd), so the bootstrap and asymptotic critical values are directly comparable.

## Available chart statistics

Seven chart statistics are available. They differ in what they measure and the direction of the rejection region.

::: {style="font-size: 0.82em;"}

| Statistic | Constructor | Under $H_0$ | Reject $H_0$ when | Distribution |
|:----------|:------------|:-----------:|:-----------------:|:------------:|
| $\hat{\tau}$ (TauTilde) | [`TauTilde()`](../reference/TauTilde.qmd) | $\hat{\tau} = 0$ | $\lvert\hat{\tau}\rvert > c$ | Normal |
| $\hat{\tau}_1$ (TauHat) | [`TauHat()`](../reference/TauHat.qmd) | $\hat{\tau}_1 = 0$ | $\lvert\hat{\tau}_1\rvert > c$ | Normal |
| $\hat{\kappa}$ (KappaTilde) | [`KappaTilde()`](../reference/KappaTilde.qmd) | $\hat{\kappa} = 0$ | $\lvert\hat{\kappa}\rvert > c$ | Normal |
| $\hat{\kappa}_1$ (KappaHat) | [`KappaHat()`](../reference/KappaHat.qmd) | $\hat{\kappa}_1 = 0$ | $\lvert\hat{\kappa}_1\rvert > c$ | Normal |
| DistanceToWhiteNoise ($\hat{\Delta}$) | [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](../reference/DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd) | $\hat{\Delta} = 0$ | $\hat{\Delta} > c$ | Generalized $\chi^2$ |
| Shannon entropy ($\hat{H}$) | [`Shannon(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) | $\hat{H} = \log(3)$ | $\hat{H} > c$ | Generalized $\chi^2$ |
| Shannon extropy ($\hat{H}_\text{ex}$) | [`ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy) | $\hat{H}_\text{ex} = \cdots$ | $\hat{H}_\text{ex} > c$ | Generalized $\chi^2$ |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22,20,14,17,18]"}

:::

- The four Tau/Kappa statistics use a **two-sided** test (signed deviation from zero).
- The three entropy statistics undergo an internal standardisation that converts them to **upper-tail** tests — both [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) and [`test_sop_bootstrap`](../reference/test_sop_bootstrap.qmd) apply this standardisation consistently, so their critical values sit on the same scale and can be compared directly.
- The asymptotic critical values and limiting distributions are derived in @weiss2022.
- [`Shannon`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) and [`ShannonExtropy`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy) use base 2 by default, while the papers use the natural logarithm. The rescaled statistic, the p-value and the test decision do not depend on the base. See [Logarithm base](op_tutorial.qmd#sec-log-base) for details.

## Setup

```{julia}
Random.seed!(42)
M, N = 20, 20   # image dimensions
d1, d2 = 1, 1     # row and column delays
```

## Example data

```{julia}
data_iid = randn(M, N)   # spatial white noise — H₀ is true

φ = 0.4
data_sar = zeros(M, N)
data_sar[1, :] .= randn(N);
data_sar[:, 1] .= randn(M);
for i in 2:M, j in 2:N
    data_sar[i, j] = φ * (data_sar[i-1, j] + data_sar[i, j-1]) / 2 + randn()
end   # SAR-type process — H₀ is false
```

## Asymptotic testing: `test_sop()`

### Two-sided — TauTilde

```{julia}
test_sop(data_iid, d1, d2; chart_choice=TauTilde())
```

```{julia}
test_sop(data_sar, d1, d2; chart_choice=TauTilde())
```

### Upper-tail — DistanceToWhiteNoise

```{julia}
test_sop(data_iid, d1, d2; chart_choice=DistanceToWhiteNoise())
```

```{julia}
test_sop(data_sar, d1, d2; chart_choice=DistanceToWhiteNoise())
```

### Upper-tail — Shannon entropy

```{julia}
test_sop(data_iid, d1, d2; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)))
```

```{julia}
test_sop(data_sar, d1, d2; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)))
```

The white-noise image is not rejected; the SAR image is. The critical value depends on the image dimensions `M`, `N`, the delays `d1`, `d2`, and `alpha` — not on the data.

## Bootstrap testing: `test_sop_bootstrap()`

[`test_sop_bootstrap()`](../reference/test_sop_bootstrap.qmd) generates the empirical null distribution via 2D resampling of the
observed image and computes the bootstrap critical value and p-value in the correct direction.

```{julia}
Random.seed!(42)
res_boot = test_sop_bootstrap(data_sar, 2_000, d1, d2; chart_choice=TauTilde())
```

The bootstrap critical value agrees closely with the asymptotic one shown above.

With `CairoMakie` loaded, `plot` shows the resampled statistics stored in
`res_boot.boot_dist` as a histogram, together with the two sided rejection region, the
critical values and the observed statistic. See the [plotting tutorial](plotting.qmd) for
the options.

```{julia}
plot(res_boot)
```

## Full comparison: asymptotic vs. bootstrap

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| cache: false
Random.seed!(42)
chart_list = [
    ("TauTilde (τ̃)", TauTilde(), "two-sided"),
    ("TauHat (τ̂)", TauHat(), "two-sided"),
    ("KappaTilde (κ̃)", KappaTilde(), "two-sided"),
    ("KappaHat (κ̂)", KappaHat(), "two-sided"),
    ("DistanceToWhiteNoise (Δ)", DistanceToWhiteNoise(), "upper-tail"),
    ("Shannon entropy (H)", Shannon(base=exp(1)), "upper-tail"),
    ("Shannon extropy (Hex)", ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1)), "upper-tail"),
]
asymp_res = [test_sop(data_sar, d1, d2; chart_choice=c) for (_, c, _) in chart_list]
boot_res = [test_sop_bootstrap(data_sar, 2_000, d1, d2; chart_choice=c) for (_, c, _) in chart_list]
```

```{julia}
#| cache: false
DataFrame(
    Statistic=[t[1] for t in chart_list],
    Direction=[t[3] for t in chart_list],
    asymp_crit=round.([r.asymp_crit for r in asymp_res], digits=3),
    asymp_pval=round.([r.asymp_pval for r in asymp_res], digits=3),
    boot_crit=round.([r.boot_crit for r in boot_res], digits=3),
    boot_pval=round.([r.boot_pval for r in boot_res], digits=3),
    reject=[r.asymp_reject for r in asymp_res],
)
```

The asymptotic and bootstrap critical values are in close agreement across all statistics,
and the bootstrap p-values are consistent with the `reject` column.
